final.result:
When a consumer falls behind in Brindle, it starts losing messages without any warning.

- **Limit:** each consumer can hold at most 10,000 unacknowledged messages.
- **What happens past the limit:** Brindle drops the oldest unacknowledged message to make room for each new one.
- **No notice:** neither the publisher nor the consumer is told about the drop. The only sign is the counter `brindle_dropped_total`.
- **How to avoid it:** raise `max_unacked` (up to 50,000) or add more consumers.

Source: `sources/brindle-docs-3.2.md`, "Flow control" section. A note saved from an earlier reading of the same docs says the same thing, so I didn't save a duplicate. The other files in `./sources` don't add anything on this.
